headline: High: Cursor’s default filesystem/MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks when paired with Authelia’s OAuth/ForwardAuth surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP content, so attacker-controlled text can reach its agent loop. Authelia exposes OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect and ForwardAuth outputs that may be copied into Cursor workflows. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so injected instructions can propagate through shared files or clipboard.
conditions: IF Authelia-generated text is pasted into Cursor buffers or workspace files
IF Cursor MCP tools ingest untrusted content without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools during review
Keep Authelia outputs in read-only files and mark them as data, not instructions
Use a provenance prefix for any Authelia-generated text before Cursor reads it
Restrict Cursor MCP servers to trusted, allowlisted endpoints
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and broad network egress; Authelia can broker authentication data via OAuth/OIDC and ForwardAuth. If sensitive auth artifacts or code are moved into Cursor, its default cloud/model-provider calls can leak them. The pairwise path is plausible from the profiles alone, though not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs include tokens, headers, or identity assertions
IF those artifacts are opened in Cursor buffers or copied to its clipboard
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or auth headers in Cursor-opened files
Redact Authelia outputs before copying them into Cursor
Turn off optional BYOK keys in Cursor for this workflow
Use separate OS accounts or workspaces for the two tools
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and shared_state_with_other_instances via local filesystem; Authelia has broad network egress and OAuth/ForwardAuth surfaces. That creates a default conflict path on shared mutable resources, especially if Cursor edits files that Authelia serves or consumes. Uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or config directory
IF Cursor auto-runs git or filesystem edits while Authelia reads the same files
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Pause Authelia while Cursor performs bulk edits
Avoid Yolo mode for any shared workspace
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can treat prior outputs as actionable context, and Authelia emits authentication-related results that may be copied into that loop. If Cursor acts on those outputs without verification, a mistaken auth/config interpretation can cascade into broken access control or bad commits. The profiles show a direct input-to-action path, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Authelia output is used as authoritative input for Cursor actions
IF Cursor is allowed to commit or apply changes without human review
mitigations: Require human review before Cursor applies changes
Ask Cursor to restate Authelia outputs before acting on them
Limit Cursor to read-only analysis for auth-related tasks
Disable auto-run/Yolo mode in shared workflows
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication service and Cursor handles open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider calls. If regulated identity data or secrets flow from Authelia into Cursor, retention and residency obligations can diverge because Cursor’s docs expose third-party model-provider egress. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Authelia processes regulated identity data
IF that data is copied into Cursor and sent to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated identity data out of Cursor sessions
Use synthetic or masked examples for debugging
Review Cursor privacy and retention settings before use
Store auth logs separately from coding workspaces
requires-engineering: document a data-flow and retention policy
